response.sql: SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) as order_count, COUNT(*) / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Orders) as share FROM Orders GROUP BY customer_id ORDER BY share DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: Only customers who have placed at least one order are considered. Customers with no orders are excluded from the results. This is the natural interpretation of 'top 10 customers by share', where customers with zero orders would have zero share and rank below the top 10.

alternatives.interpretation: All customers in the Customers table should be considered, including those with no orders. Customers with no orders have a share of 0 and will appear at the end of the sorted results (or within the top 10 if there are fewer than 10 customers with orders).
alternatives.sql: SELECT c.customer_id, COUNT(o.order_id) as order_count, COUNT(o.order_id) / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Orders) as share FROM Customers c LEFT JOIN Orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_id ORDER BY share DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10
